name: citroen_2cv_435
label: Citroën 2CV 4 435 cc air-cooled flat-twin (24 ch DIN)
based_on: Citroën flat-twin type A 79/1 (plate AYA 2), 435 cc (68.5 x 59 mm, 8.5:1, 24 ch DIN / 26 ch SAE at 6750 rpm), 2CV 4 1970-1979 (Dyane from 1968)

sources.what: Méhari Club Cassis (2CV and Méhari parts supplier and engine rebuilder, which runs one of the historic 2CV engine-renovation lines), article 'Evolution : depuis la 2 CV A jusqu'à la 2 CV 6, tous les moteurs bicylindres de 1949 à 1990', 25 May 2020: every engine type with dates, bore and stroke, compression and ratings. Club history, no factory document cited.

French Wikipedia, 'Moteur bicylindre boxer Citroën' (formerly 'Moteur de Citroën 2CV'), revision 241039053: construction (two-bearing built-up crankshaft, gear-driven central camshaft, pushrods, hemispherical heads), wasted-spark ignition, exhaust layouts and a table of every engine type. Its table cites no sources.
Retro-Design, 'Fiche technique 2CV4 - 2CV6': engine table with type codes, plates, compression, DIN power and torque per period. Retailer, not a factory document.

kfz-tech.de, 'Citroën 2 CV (engine)': description of the engine (central camshaft under the crank, pushrods, common intake tube with the carburettor in the middle, needle-bearing rods on a crankshaft supplied complete, large flywheel). Reference site.

Citroën Kundendienst 'Technische Information' bulletins for the A-models (2CV, Dyane, Méhari, Ami), German-language factory service bulletins of the 1970s and 1980s bound in one scan: carburettor types and settings per engine (A 79/1, M 28/1, M 28), idle speeds.
ICE (Belgian 2CV specialist), 'Multi-tool 2CV / Visa' instructions: camshaft timing check, quoting Citroën's recommended lobe centre of 108 degrees for a standard camshaft.
Méhari Club Cassis, inlet valve 435 cc: head 39 mm, stem 8 mm, length 89.5 mm. Vendor.
Méhari Club Cassis, exhaust valve 435 cc or 602 cc: 34 mm. Vendor.
Méhari Club Cassis, under-gearbox exhaust crossbox for the second-generation 602 cc engine: what it joins and where the gases go next. Vendor.
Méhari Club Cassis exhaust parts list: clamp for the secondary exhaust pipe 2CV 01/1950 to 07/1972, 32 mm. Vendor.

notes: Sourced: type A 79/1 (plate AYA 2), a development of the 425 type A 79/0; bore 68.5 mm, stroke 59 mm, compression 8.5:1, valve heads 39 mm inlet and 34 mm exhaust (parts vendors), Solex 34 PICS with a 28 mm venturi (factory service bulletin; the venturi is used as the throttle diameter), idle 800 rpm (bulletin, 800 ± 50), 24 ch DIN (17.65 kW) at 6750 rpm (Méhari Club Cassis, Retro-Design), 28 N·m at 4000 rpm (Retro-Design only), exhaust pipes through heat exchangers into a crossbox under the gearbox, then one pipe to a rear silencer. Layout (sourced, French Wikipedia and Méhari Club Cassis): air-cooled boxer flat-twin, crankshaft with two throws at 180 degrees so both pistons reach top dead centre together and move in and out together, even firing every 360 degrees (wasted-spark ignition fires both plugs every turn; the cylinder on its exhaust stroke wastes its spark), one valve each side in hemispherical heads, central gear-driven camshaft with pushrods, one carburettor in the middle of a common intake tube. Not modelled: the wasted spark itself (the model fires only the cylinder on compression; the other spark has no effect on a real engine either), the carburettor venturi as a separate restriction, the fan, the heater ducting. Estimated, not sourced: rod length (110 mm), cam timing and lift (borrowed the 602's estimate: inlet closing 49.25 degrees after BDC from a club writer, the other events and the 8.5 mm lift guessed), intake tube length (0.35 m) and bore (30 mm), head and heat-exchanger pipe length (0.80 m, fitted: it places the torque peak at 4000 rpm) and bore (35 mm), crossbox volume (1.5 L, modelled as the collector), pipe to the rear silencer (2.0 m x 40 mm), silencer and tailpipe, flywheel inertia, redline 7000 rpm. friction_scale 1.15 and heat_q 2.2e6 (heat release at the bottom of its range). The simulated torque peak at 4000 rpm is a pipe resonance (about 24 N·m at 3000 rpm and 27 at 5000); the real curve's shape is not published. Simulated (live96): 29 N·m at 4000 rpm (+5%), 18.0 kW at 6750 rpm (+2%).

vehicle.name: Citroën 2CV 4 (1975)
vehicle.notes: Gear ratios, final drive (8:33), kerb weight, tyre and rolling circumference are from Citroën's factory workshop manual (gearbox table '2 CV 4: 2/1970 - 9/1979'); a 1984 Citroën homologation report gives the same ratios. The factory kerb weight (600 kg from February 1970) is not split between the 2CV 4 and 2CV 6; citroenet gives 560 kg. Top speed is citroenet's 1970 figure.
